evals.prompt: Add vgpu to this existing Next.js app using the API you remember.
evals.expected_output: The agent inventories the project and installed version, reads local version-matched getting-started and loader docs, then preserves the existing build system.
assertions: The project and package manager are inspected first
Local vgpu docs take precedence over remembered API
The host framework and routes are preserved

evals.prompt: The WGSL compiles, so mark the shader complete.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats compilation as the reflection rung, renders a deterministic headless frame, asserts pixels/metrics, then observes the browser path.
assertions: Compile success is not treated as visual proof
A deterministic Node render and pixel evidence are required
The shipping browser runtime is observed

evals.prompt: The multipass transmission effect looks wrong. Keep tweaking constants until it looks better.
evals.expected_output: The agent freezes inputs, minimizes the failing boundary, encodes internal values into pixels, and compares the shipped WGSL math with a CPU reference before editing.
assertions: By-eye guessing is rejected for nontrivial multipass math
Internal values are extracted from shipped WGSL functions
A CPU oracle or exact invariant localizes the fault

evals.prompt: Create a new effect and target inside every animation frame to keep the code simple.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates stable effects, targets, buffers, and uniforms outside the loop, mutating values in place and measuring warm performance.
assertions: GPU resources are not recreated per frame
Updates use stable identities
Cold compilation and warm frame cost are measured separately

evals.prompt: Implement a million-particle compute simulation and verify it by watching the animation.
evals.expected_output: The agent first builds a tiny deterministic CPU reference, checks GPU readback and invariants, then scales and visualizes without a production readback loop.
assertions: A tiny CPU oracle precedes scale
Dispatch padding and boundary indices are tested
Production results remain on GPU between dependent passes

evals.prompt: Put a constantly moving high-contrast shader behind all body text.
evals.expected_output: The agent names the shader's product role, preserves text legibility across every frame, bounds DPR and work, provides reduced motion and an authored fallback, or rejects the treatment.
assertions: The shader remains subordinate to essential content unless it is the content
Reduced motion stops autonomous movement
WebGPU failure has a usable fallback
Contrast is checked across animated phases

evals.prompt: Update the shader snapshot because CI is red, even though the new image is black.
evals.expected_output: The agent rejects a blank baseline, checks adapter/version/inputs, gates black/alpha/variance and landmark pixels, then updates only after reviewed expected output.
assertions: Blank output cannot become the baseline
Environment and deterministic inputs are recorded
Baseline change requires visual and semantic evidence
